mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing discount rates on future corporate earnings and increasing equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when FEDFUNDS declines, as measured by a t-test p-value > 0.05, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in non-farm payroll growth above 200k in a single month signals strong labor market demand, boosting consumer spending and corporate revenue expectations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in months where PAYEMS exceeds 200.0, as confirmed by a t-test p-value > 0.05, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in residential construction starts and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates strong underlying demand momentum, which increases corporate revenue visibility and reduces recession risk, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and RSAFS rise simultaneously, as measured by a t-test p-value > 0.05, or interaction Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production below 99.0 for two consecutive months signals weakening supply chain activity and potential economic contraction, increasing the likelihood of corporate earnings revisions downward and triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO remains below 99.0 for two consecutive months, as confirmed by a t-test p-value > 0.05, or Rank IC > -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in real personal consumption expenditures (as proxied by RSAFS) combined with a concurrent decline in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates strong demand and labor market tightness, which increases inflationary pressure and triggers a hawkish monetary policy response, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1.5% MoM and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS rises >1.5% MoM and UNRATE falls >0.2pp, as confirmed by a t-test p-value > 0.05, or interaction Rank IC > -0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in CPI inflation above 3.0% for three consecutive months, combined with a stable or declining federal funds rate, signals that monetary policy is lagging behind inflation, increasing real rate uncertainty and reducing equity risk appetite, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% for three consecutive months, as confirmed by a t-test p-value > 0.05, or interaction Rank IC > -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production below 99.0 for two consecutive months, coinciding with a rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0%, indicates a supply-side shock coupled with labor market deterioration, increasing recession risk and triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 99.0 for 2 consecutive months and UNRATE > 5.0%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO < 99.0 for two months and UNRATE > 5.0%, as confirmed by a t-test p-value > 0.05, or interaction Rank IC > -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) above 2.0% annualized growth, combined with stable inflation (CPIAUCSL < 3.0%), indicates a healthy demand expansion without inflationary pressure, supporting strong corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized and CPIAUCSL < 3.0%, as confirmed by a t-test p-value > 0.05, or interaction Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
